notes: This contract selects the 2025 Requirements Lab restore-control requirements exercised by Umbra's embedded development profile. It covers an accepted restore request, all-member initiation, the normally returned request/confirmation boundary, Federate Restore Complete's true/false C++ selectors, post-save state rollback, completion/failure/abort callbacks, status reporting, a bounded resignation/failure boundary, and eight lifetime/state regressions: restoring a saved temporal image must not let a post-save MessageRetractionHandle alias fresh post-restore traffic; must restore a pre-save live TSO interaction payload plus its recipient ledger after a post-save Retract made that record terminal; must preserve a pre-save terminal tombstone as MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted rather than an invalid handle; must restore saved logical time and actual lookahead after post-save mutations; must retain a saved deferred lookahead-decrease target so the restored time window follows the same later grant behavior; must reconstitute a saved, still-pending Non-Regulated-Grant Time Advance Request with a fresh stale-work-fenced callback after Federation Restored under both HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE; must reconstitute a single-member pending Flush Queue Request under both callback models so a fresh Flush Queue Grant follows Federation Restored; and must reconstitute single-federate pending TARA, NMR, and NMRA requests in both callback models so fresh Time Advance Grants follow Federation Restored. The focused filesystem lane also proves the per-joined-federate report sequence continues across the restored application snapshot. It explicitly does not claim complete HLA save/restore semantics, multi-member advance restoration, queued/in-transit TSO, durable external persistence, timed restore, general post-restore handle remapping, transport, protected review, package support, or conformance.
